South America: Demerara, Rupununi, Essequibo and Cuyuni River basins. Type locality: Wismar, British Guiana.

Auchenipterus demerarae has a wide range of distribution and is known from the Demerara River, Essequibo River and its tributaries, the Rupununi River in Guyana, and the Botanamo River of the Rio Cuyuni system in Venezuela. The extent of occurrence (EOO) is estimated at 104,392 km2 and the area of occupancy (AOO) at 11,128 km2. The overall area of the distribution seems relatively well preserved, despite local impacts of mining activities in Cuyuni River, but there are no apparent risks to the species. Thus, it is assessed as Least Concern (LC) due to its wide distribution and the lack of any known major threats (IUCN 2022).

Auchenipterus demerarae is most similar in appearance to A. nuchalus (Spix & Agassiz, 1829) but with a lateral band on the body. The sides of the body are peppered with very fine spots with a dark median band from the gill-opening to the caudal. The dorsal and caudal are dusky. The tip of the upper caudal lobe is sometimes quite dark, the lower fin is hyaline.

Etymology: The specific name demerarae (Dutch: Demerary) is a historical region in the Guianas on the north coast of South America which is now part of the country of Guyana. Of the Demerara River, presumably the type locality in Wismar, Guyana.
